At the time of inspection, the facility did not have the records of acquisition for two owl monkeys and one cotton-top
tamarin or the records of disposition for two kookaburra.
Records containing the required information for animals disposed of, or acquired for, use in regulated activities (including
those offspring born on premises) are necessary to accurately track animals to ensure their humane care and use.
Records must be maintained, which fully and correctly disclose all the required information concerning all animals
purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, leased, transported, sold, euthanized or otherwise disposed of and shall
include any offspring born or hatched while in the licensee’s possession.

citations.desc: Access and inspection of records and property; submission of itineraries.
citations.narrative:
At the time of inspection, the licensee was unable to furnish a copy of their contingency plan.
Per this section, all documents that are required to be kept under the Animal Welfare Act (AWA) should be available at
the time of an inspection so the required documents can be reviewed to determine compliance with the provisions of the
AWA. Failure to provide documents and records prevents APHIS officials from verifying compliance with the provisions of
the AWA. Copies of all documents and records required under the AWA must be on the premises and available for
review.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The facility does not have an effective program for the control of roaches. In the large building housing a majority of the
marmosets and tamarins, the inspector saw numerous roaches in clusters along the ceiling. The inspector also saw
roaches clustered around an outlet inside the kitchen where food is prepped and stored. While the facility does take steps
to manage roaches, the current pest control plan is not effective.
Pests such as roaches can spread disease and contaminate food, surfaces, and animal housing areas. An effective
program for the control of insects, external parasites affecting nonhuman primates, and birds and mammals that are
pests, must be established and maintained so as to promote the health and well-being of the animals and reduce
contamination by pests in animal areas.
This is a 1st Re-License Inspection for a Class “A” license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within 2 more inspections or by September 7, 2026 or the applicant will forfeit the license
fee and must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires.
